shared_elements: upright monolithic stone slab with rounded top and tapering base
anthropomorphic figure carved in low relief on a single face
head/face zone at the top with hollowed eye-like depressions
paired arm-like elements flanking a central torso
raised vertical ridge/median line down the body
museum display of the stone standing free on a plinth
justification: Both are upright, roughly rectangular stone slabs bearing a single bilaterally symmetrical anthropomorphic figure in shallow relief, with a face zone at the top, arm-like elements curving down either side of a raised central axis, and a plain lower zone — a genuinely comparable compositional scheme. The decisive difference is execution and legibility: A carries crisp, deliberate incised detail (a prominent central disc, encircling bands, patterned headgear), whereas B is reduced to soft, pitted hollows and swellings with no linear ornament at all, so it reads as a much cruder or heavily weathered rendering.
